minor.issue: Still fully synchronous (audio extract + N Whisper chunks + fallback pass + GPT-5.6-terra + storage). For 37.78s toe-source it took ~35-40s wall time on preview - safely under the ~100s ingress cap here but a longer 90-120s upload could still trip 502. critical_code_review_comments: caption_ai._split_wav: offset is recomputed from len(frames)/framerate but with `max(1, sampwidth*nchannels*framerate)` in the denominator that is byte-based, not frame-based. In practice wave.readframes returns FRAMES worth of bytes = frames*sampwidth*nchannels, so len(frames)/(sampwidth*nchannels*framerate) does equal seconds — but the max(1, ...) guard hides a bug if params are ever zero. Prefer offset += frames_read / framerate computed via source.tell() to avoid subtle drift on multichannel input.

caption_ai._build_candidate: 'trustworthy = words and average_logprob > -1.45' - Whisper on short 10-sec chunks with clean speech regularly returns avg_logprob around -0.30 to -0.60, so this threshold is generous. If a run does hit -1.45 (music/silence), the ngram/bigram guards also fire, so the belt-and-suspenders is fine. Just document why -1.45 was chosen.

caption_ai.transcribe_words: raises ValueError('No trustworthy transcript was found...') which /projects/process wraps to HTTP 424. Good user-facing message. Consider also including transcription diagnostics in the 424 body so the UI can show 'try re-uploading in a quieter section' etc.
captions.process_video: still exposes provider error text via HTTPException(424, f'Caption generation failed: {str(exc)[:180]}') - fine for testing, sanitize before production shipping.

captions.retranscribe_project: does NOT re-check duration<=120 on the re-listen path. Since the source came from a project that was originally accepted, this is safe, but a defensive re-assert would future-proof against direct DB mutation.

caption_ai.convert_to_hinglish: 'len(converted) < max(1, int(len(words) * .8))' safeguards structure, but if GPT returns exactly 80% of indices it silently keeps the missing indices as the raw Devanagari original in words[].text. This is the correct fallback but it means text may still contain some Devanagari on partial failure - the test at the moment finds none, so the model complied.
captions.py exceeds the 700-line advisory: still under 300 here (283 lines), fine.
UploadStage: 'video/quicktime' MOV files - inspect() only checks filename regex (.mp4|.mov), not MIME. Fine, backend also validates by suffix.
TranscriptPanel: renders `word.uncertain ? ? : word.important && ` - if a word is BOTH important and uncertain, only the '?' shows. Product may want both (color + '?'). Minor UX.

Backend regression: cd /app/backend && REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview_url> python -m pytest tests/test_toe_protector_iter3.py -v. Costs ONE real /projects/process (~35s) + ONE real /projects/{id}/retranscribe (~35s) on toe-protector-source.mp4 (37.78s / 8.6MB). Unit tests in TestRepetitionGuard are free. UNLIMITED_TESTING=true and STRIPE_MODE=unavailable_country still in backend/.env. Iteration_1 (16 tests) and iteration_2 (7 tests) suites remain valid. The 'usable/coherent with uncertainty visible' bar mentioned in the RCA is respected in the assertions - we require adaptive-chunked mode, ngram_repeat<3, coverage>=35s of 37.78s, >=6 of the ad-vocab terms, Roman Hinglish shape, and the absence of the catastrophic loop, but we DO NOT demand perfect verbatim.
rca of the issue: Root cause (as documented by main agent E1 and confirmed here): the original pipeline sent the full 37.78s audio to Whisper with forced language='hi' and no chunking, causing a repeated-phrase hallucination during music-only segments where Whisper looped 'यूट्यूब प्रोटेक्टर'. Fix stack in caption_ai.py + captions.py: (1) _split_wav slices the WAV into 10-second chunks; (2) _transcription_pass runs primary language then optional fallback per chunk; (3) _build_candidate discards segments with no_speech_prob>=0.65, computes 2-gram / 4-gram / unique_ratio penalties, and rejects trustworthy on ngram_repeat>=3, unique_ratio<0.24, bigram_ratio>0.30; (4) transcribe_words picks the max-score trustworthy candidate per chunk and applies the same guards to the overall stitched transcript, raising a graceful ValueError if the whole clip is untrustworthy; (5) convert_to_hinglish emits per-word 'uncertain' markers for genuinely garbled tokens. Reproduction: pytest TestRepetitionGuard::test_repetition_metrics_reject_youtube_protector_loop and ::test_candidate_marked_not_trustworthy_on_loop cover the guard directly with the exact catastrophic input; TestToeProtectorRealPipeline::test_no_catastrophic_repetition_in_raw covers the end-to-end path with the actual 37.78s source. Mitigation status: FIXED. Two phrases around 20-30s remain imperfect but surface via uncertain=True on the affected words (schema-level; count logged, not asserted, because the exact indices vary run-to-run).
